sentences.text:
The instant petition is directed against the order dated 24.06.2023, by which the competent authority has rejected the objections filed by the petitioners under Section 3C of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act').

sentences.text: The objection of the petitioners was that the respondents had proposed to acquire more land on one side of the road, whereas they should have acquired equal area on both sides from the centre of the road.
The objection has been rejected observing that the proposal for acquisition of the land was prepared after survey and joint inspection.

4. The scheme of the Act reveals that under Section 3A, the Central Government if satisfied that any land is required for a public purpose, it has to issue a notification in this behalf declaring its intention to acquire such land.

5. Under sub-section(1) of Section 3C of the Act, "any person interested in the land, is conferred the right to file objection to the use of the land for the purpose or purposes mentioned in that sub-section".
Thus, the objection could only be in respect of the proposed user of the land sought to be acquired.
The objections filed by the petitioners does not fall within the scope of enquiry under Section 3C of the Act.

Moreover, the order passed by the competent authority under sub-section (1)
of Section 3C of the Act, has been made final.

6. In face of the finding recorded by the competent authority that the proposed land alone is needed for public purpose as per survey carried out by the joint inspection team, no ground is made out to interfere with the said order.
7.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has also pressed relief no. 3, which is for a mandamus directing the respondents to award compensation to the petitioners for having acquired their land.
8. On query made by the Court as to whether notification under Section 3D of the Act has been made or not, learned counsel for the petitioners feigned ignorance.
9. The law itself stipulates that after notification under Section 3D of the Act, the respondents are under mandate of law to make award.
Consequently, no direction is required to be issued at this stage.
10. The petition lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
(Donadi Ramesh, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 19.9.2023/
